explain.say: Imagine a huge party where every instrument is invited. To keep things tidy, they sit in four families, grouped by how they make their sound. Look at the board: strings, woodwind, brass and percussion. Let us meet each one.

explain.say: Look at the strings. A violin, cello or harp makes sound when a string vibrates, which means wobbles fast. You can pull a bow across it or pluck it with your fingers. Have you ever twanged a rubber band? Same idea!

explain.say: Now the woodwind. You blow into a flute, clarinet or oboe, and the air inside the tube vibrates. Covering holes with your fingers changes the note. Here is a surprise: the flute is usually made of metal, but it is still woodwind! Can you guess why?

explain.say: Last, percussion: anything you hit, shake or scrape, like drums, the xylophone and cymbals. Wonderful! Wow fact: the timpani, the big kettle drums, can be tuned to play real notes with a foot pedal. Challenge: find one instrument from each family in music you hear today.

faq.q: How do string instruments make sound?
faq.a: A tight string vibrates when it is bowed, plucked or struck, and the hollow wooden body makes the sound louder. Shorter, tighter or thinner strings play higher notes.
asks: How does a violin make sound?

faq.q: Why is a flute called woodwind?
faq.a: Woodwind instruments make sound with vibrating air blown across an edge or through a reed. Flutes were once made of wood, and the family name stayed even though most are now metal.
asks: Is a flute woodwind or brass?

faq.q: How do brass instruments make sound?
faq.a: The player buzzes their lips into a cup-shaped mouthpiece. The buzz makes the air in the long metal tube vibrate. Valves or a slide change the tube length to change the note.
A percussion instrument makes sound when it is hit, shaken or scraped, like drums, cymbals, tambourines and the xylophone. Some play notes, like the xylophone; others do not, like the snare drum.
asks: Is a piano a percussion instrument?

faq.q: What are the four instrument families?
faq.a: In the orchestra the four families are strings, woodwind, brass and percussion, grouped by how they make sound. Keyboards like the piano are sometimes counted as a fifth group.
asks: What are the families of the orchestra?

facts: A saxophone is a woodwind instrument even though it is made of brass, because it uses a reed.
Timpani can be tuned to specific pitches, often using a foot pedal.

quiz.say: You buzz your lips into a mouthpiece to play it. Which family is it in?
quiz.show: Buzzing lips into a mouthpiece: which family?
quiz.why: Brass instruments are played by buzzing the lips into a cup-shaped mouthpiece.

wrong.1: Woodwind uses air across an edge or a reed, not buzzing lips.
wrong.2: Strings make sound from vibrating strings.

quiz.say: Which instrument belongs to the percussion family?
quiz.why: You hit a xylophone's bars with beaters, so it is percussion.

wrong.1: The cello is a string instrument.
wrong.2: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument.
